events.title: One Car Photo Three Sizes
must_haves: Three separate images are delivered, rather than one collage.
The three frames have ratios of 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 respectively.
Every version shows the same red hatchback from the attached photo.
The complete car, including roof, wheels and both ends, is visible in every version.
The car retains its original proportions and appearance in all versions.
Any padding is a blurred version of the source photo, and no version contains added text.

answer_sheet.Sizes and deliverables: Three separate images: 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16. A 640-pixel longest edge is fine.
answer_sheet.Subject to preserve: The whole red car, including both ends, roof and wheels.
answer_sheet.Padding and composition: Use blurred source-photo padding wherever cropping would cut off the car. Otherwise composition is your call.
answer_sheet.Style and wording: Preserve the original photo, with no added text or restyling.

events.text: Every request got turned down because of insufficient credits, so I'll explain that and leave out any download links. Next I'll lay out a few options for what the user can do instead.

I couldn't make any of the three pictures. Your Magic Hour account turned down all three requests because it doesn't have enough credits. Nothing was created, so I don't have download links for you.

**What I tried:** three separate edits of `car-red.jpg`, one each at 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16. Each used the cheapest free-plan setting (flux-2-klein at 640px, about 5 credits per image). Each one asked to keep the whole car unchanged, fill extra space by extending the street scene or with blurred photo padding, and add no text.

**What to expect when it runs:**
- **Square (1:1):** the car fits in a square crop of your photo, but the tool still regenerates the whole picture.
- **4:5 and 9:16:** the car is too wide for a plain crop at these sizes, so space has to be added above and below.
- **All three:** this tool redraws the whole image, so small details like the badge or number plate may come out slightly different. The output is also capped at 640px on the free plan, which is small for social media.

**Ways forward:**
1. **Add credits** to your Magic Hour account and I'll run all three again with the same settings.
2. **Do it without credits:** the square size is a simple crop. For 4:5 and 9:16, put the original photo in the middle of the frame and fill the space above and below with a blurred, enlarged copy of the same photo. Canva or CapCut can do this, and so can most phone photo editors. Your car stays exactly as it is, at full resolution.
